cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Return to the First Hope
cards.instruction: Return to an early hope after every setback, expanding its meaning until the whole scene seems to fulfill it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I pulled the plug when the sound man did. This concert was meant to bring the village together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He unplugged a faulty microphone. You unplugged the stage supply, lights and sound together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, clearing the sound. We'll hear each other sing now.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Half the audience has gone home for torches. They want to read the song sheets.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask them to light a neighbour's sheet as well as their own. That's the village together, even before the chorus.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copied unplugging threatens the togetherness hope; A3 covers lost system as clearer shared voices; A5 turns B4 torches into neighbors helping each other participate.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 lights-and-sound loss now explains both A3 acoustic singing and B4 need for light; B4 shared sheets supplies A5 request.

relationship.evidence: B4 audience voluntarily helps rather than being made obstructive for escalation.

heightening.evidence: A5 finds the original hope already happening through B4 workaround before the planned song even begins.

specificity.evidence: B2 explicitly identifies both affected systems, repairing the unsupported darkness assumption.
